root_cause.text: `isofs_export_iget()` in the ISOFS NFS export path trusted attacker-controlled block numbers from the file handle and only checked for `block == 0`, allowing `isofs_iget()`/`sb_bread()` to be invoked on arbitrary in-range blocks instead of validating them against `ISOFS_SB(sb)->s_nzones`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that `isofs_fh_to_dentry()` and `isofs_fh_to_parent()` pass `ifid->block`/`ifid->parent_block` into `isofs_export_iget()`, which “only rejects block == 0 before calling isofs_iget() and ultimately sb_bread()”; the patch changes this to `if (block == 0 || block >= ISOFS_SB(sb)->s_nzones) return ERR_PTR(-ESTALE);`, showing the missing upper-bound validation was the flaw.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description states that `isofs_fh_to_dentry()` and `isofs_fh_to_parent()` pass `ifid->block`/`ifid->parent_block` into `isofs_export_iget()`, which “only rejects block == 0 before calling isofs_iget() and ultimately sb_bread()”; the patch changes this to `if (block == 0 || block >= ISOFS_SB(sb)->s_nzones) return ERR_PTR(-ESTALE);`, showing the missing upper-bound validation was the flaw.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject invalid ISOFS export block numbers outside the valid zone range to avoid improper inode lookup.
intent_record.what: The `isofs_export_iget()` function’s early validity check was changed from rejecting only `block == 0` to rejecting both `block == 0` and any `block >= ISOFS_SB(sb)->s_nzones`, returning `ERR_PTR(-ESTALE)` in those cases before calling `isofs_iget()`.
intent_record.how: This prevents the code from attempting to look up or export inodes whose block number is outside the filesystem’s valid zone range, avoiding invalid access and ensuring out-of-range NFS/export requests fail with stale-handle semantics.

grouping_result.intent: Reject invalid ISOFS export block numbers outside the valid zone range to avoid improper inode lookup.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds validation for ISOFS export block numbers to reject out-of-range values instead of trusting attacker-controlled blocks in the NFS export path.

candidates.rationale: This is the only pre-fix validation in isofs_export_iget(), and it is insufficient because it rejects only block 0 while still allowing attacker-controlled in-range blocks that should have been validated against the ISOFS zone limit.

This statement performs inode lookup using the unchecked block value from the file handle, which is the direct manifestation of the bug: arbitrary in-range blocks can reach isofs_iget()/sb_bread() without validation against s_nzones.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line uses the attacker-controlled block value from the NFS file handle to perform inode lookup without validating it against ISOFS_SB(sb)->s_nzones, which is the root cause of the vulnerability.
This is the only pre-fix check on the export block number, but it only rejects block 0 and fails to constrain the value to the valid ISOFS zone range, allowing arbitrary in-range blocks to proceed.
